citation: Sibiya BP (2018). Black tax and the vulnerability of the emerging middle class. MBA research report, University of Pretoria (GIBS)

claims.text: Because parents sacrificed and the family endured hardship to get one where one is, the debt is felt as guilt rather than as a stated obligation, so giving to family continues even when it is not required, and any new product or policy is read through whether it relieves family need.
evaluative_rules: Weigh a purchase by whether it relieves family need before it serves you
objections: Does this help my family, or does it only help me?

claims.text: Because relatives lack income and basic needs, being prosperous or comfortable while family suffers is not possible, so family support is prioritised over personal consumption and investment, and a new product or policy is treated as legitimate only if it does not appear to benefit the individual at the family's expense.
evaluative_rules: Judge a purchase by whether it can be justified while family is in need
objections: How would it look if I spent on this while my siblings cannot afford school fees?
vocabulary: cannot be seen going on holiday

claims.text: Because support is embedded in an Ubuntu worldview and an extended family structure, it is lived as a shared way of life rather than a communicated obligation or tax, so contribution happens automatically and unspoken, and a new product or policy is read through whether it fits the collective family setup rather than individual gain.
evaluative_rules: Judge a product by whether it fits the larger family setup, not the individual
objections: Does this fit how our family does things, or does it pull me out of it?

claims.text: Because birth order and family tradition place responsibility automatically on the first born or the successful member, spending continues on siblings' education until they are independent, and a new product or policy is read as a means to discharge that role obligation.
evaluative_rules: Judge a product by whether it helps discharge the role obligation to dependants
objections: Does this help me get my younger brother independent?

claims.text: Because the arrangement is felt as unfair yet inescapable, giving continues despite resentment, and a new product or policy is met with ambivalence, weighed against its emotional cost.
evaluative_rules: Weigh a purchase against the emotional cost it carries, not only its price
objections: Will this add to the burden I already carry?

confidence: One qualitative South African study: 18 in-depth interviews with employed emerging middle-class people (12 African, 3 Indian, 1 Coloured by the author's count). Mechanisms durable; magnitudes and prevalence unknown.
subject: employed middle-class people who support parents, siblings and extended family from their salary (black tax), and weigh any new spending against what the family needs
year_note: Interviews over two months in 2018 for a University of Pretoria (GIBS) MBA report.
